doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Instruments played, later reunion records, and the retrospective
summary: He doubled many instruments, recorded with the band through 1965, and heard a Sauter retrospective.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah. So in your tenure in that band you played oboe and tenor sax—
Flute, piccolo, clarinet, and Nick Travis used to travel with the bass player and if a car got stuck on the road I’d wind up playing bass with the band. What an experience.
Well you were a good guy to have around.
Well I felt great being on that band. It was a privilege. I’m the luckiest man in the world that I was a performing musician on that band.
So after that, what five years, four or five years—

Four or five years. Well it goes beyond that because after the band broke up we recorded in ‘57 and ‘59 and ‘61 and ‘65. And I made most of the records with the band. One album I didn’t make. One album I did half of it, but the last day was done by my replacement so he got his name on the album. I don’t care about that, I know I was there.
You knew you were there. Do you still listen to those records?

Once in a while. Once in a while. I’m surprised they play it on the radio. About three months ago they had a forty hour retrospective on Eddie Sauter and they played everything he ever wrote for the band in New York City. And a friend of mine recorded the whole thing and sent me tapes of the whole show, complete with stories.
